title: Orange Semifreddo with Dark Chocolate
changes_from_base: A hot-syrup meringue with orange zest replaces the whisked whole-egg base, and grated dark chocolate replaces the jam swirl.
summary: Orange-scented semifreddo on a light Italian meringue, flecked with grated dark chocolate.

ingredients.item: large egg whites, at room temperature

ingredients.note: 100 g for the syrup, 25 g for the whites
45 g folded in, 15 g to finish

steps.title: Line
steps.text: Line the 1.5 litre loaf tin with cling film leaving an 8 cm overhang and place it in the freezer. Put the 3 large egg whites into the stand mixer bowl.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip the 240 ml double cream to soft peaks using the stand mixer with whisk, then cover and chill.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Warm 60 ml water and 100 g caster sugar on low without stirring until dissolved for about 4 min, then boil on medium-high towards 114 °C in the small saucepan.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: When the syrup reaches 99 °C, whisk the whites on medium until frothy. Add 1 tsp of the 25 g sugar, whisk on high to soft peaks, then add the rest of the 25 g a little at a time.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: At 114 °C, with the mixer on medium-high, pour the syrup in a thin stream down the side of the bowl, away from the whisk. Keep whisking until glossy, doubled and cooled to room temperature, 4-5 min, then beat in the orange zest and vanilla.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Stir in a third of the whipped cream, fold in the remaining cream with 45 g dark chocolate, spread the mixture into the tin, cover with film, and freeze at least 8 h.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Unmould the semifreddo, scatter the remaining 15 g dark chocolate over the top, slice and serve at once.

tips: Grate the chocolate straight from the fridge so it stays in fine flakes.
Clip the thermometer to the pan before the syrup starts to boil so you catch 114 °C exactly.
Blood orange zest gives a deeper colour and a slightly berry-like note.
storage: Wrap well and keep in the freezer up to 2 weeks; slice straight from the freezer with a hot, dry knife.
